subject: Coffee & Tea
title: How Britain Fell in Love With Tea
description: A fast breakdown of How Britain Fell in Love With Tea for builders.

hook.text: Britain drinks 100 million cups of tea every day—more per capita than almost anywhere except Turkey and Ireland.

buildup.text: Tea arrived in England in the 1660s when Catherine of Braganza—a Portuguese princess—married Charles II.

discovery.text: Catherine brought her tea-drinking habit to court. The aristocracy copied the queen, and tea became fashionable overnight.

twist.text: Tea was initially so expensive that families kept it in locked wooden chests—the original 'tea caddies.'

climax.text: As prices dropped in the 1800s, tea went from luxury to necessity. Even factory workers got tea breaks.

punchline.text: A queen's habit became a nation's identity. Britain runs on tea.

quiz.question: Who popularized tea in the English court?
options: Catherine of Braganza, wife of Charles II
